summary: A single global terminal-label state file was shared by all concurrent sessions, so labels collided across sessions.
A command file referenced a best-practices document filename that did not exist, so the read failed before a fallback search.
Hooks and Bash subprocesses derived different session IDs, so label set wrote one state file and restore read another, overwriting the new label.
A shipped systemd service file hardcoded one developer's absolute paths, so the service failed to start from any other checkout location.
Project docs told users to install commands into a user-level directory where they were not picked up, so slash commands were unavailable.
MCP server setup left out the client configuration file, so the server ran but Claude Code could not discover or connect to it.
Terminal-label restore was unreliable because one override file was shared by all terminals, subprocess TTY detection failed, and a stat flag was Linux-only.
The init wizard left the MCP server stack unconfigured, and docs referenced a server directory and port that did not exist in the repo.
A command file hardcoded one developer's absolute path to a document, so the read failed on every other installation.
A library package named after a stdlib module shadowed it when placed on PYTHONPATH, breaking unrelated code that imported the stdlib module.
MCP servers ran under systemd but their client registration had been lost, one lacked a health endpoint, and a service directive sat in the wrong section.
The issue-claim command rejected a well-formed invocation with a usage error, so claiming a new worktree issue failed.
A browser snapshot tool called a Playwright page attribute that the installed library no longer provided, so every snapshot call errored.
The session cleanup command removed only the first stale session and then exited with a misleading unavailable message.
The coordination MCP server failed a status call with a stdlib import error from its Python environment.
A package's pyproject referenced a README file that did not exist, so dependency sync failed at build.
A package lacked wheel build configuration for its source layout, so dependency sync still failed after the README fix.
A system service file lacked a user directive, so the service ran as root with a read-only home and could not create its cache directory.
The second-opinion server crashed at startup initializing its model client on a very new Python version with the pinned SDK.
Dead sessions stayed in the coordination registry for a day or more although the documented staleness model said abandoned sessions are auto-released.
A worktree listing showed worktrees whose folders were gone, and many merged local branches were never cleaned up after their work landed.
Session tool calling silently made no tool calls with a newer model and returned a failure message while reporting success.
The lint target reported many pre-existing errors, including an undefined name that would fail at runtime, which had accumulated unaddressed.
Second-opinion MCP tools all failed with a parameter-validation error when the server was not actually running, hiding the real cause.
The deck generator named the source communication framework in slide content and footers, which the owner considered unnecessary attribution.
Every second-opinion MCP tool returned an invalid-parameters error, apparently because the server process was not starting, blocking review workflows.
The second-opinion skill told the agent to pass a model argument to a tool that does not accept one, so non-default model requests failed.
Base64 image payloads were decoded without size limits and errors were swallowed by a bare exception handler, risking memory exhaustion.
Slide validation regexes and substring term matching were over-broad and flagged ordinary text such as email addresses as placeholders or banned terms.
The diagram tool's save path failed with permission denied because the containerised server could not write to host filesystem paths.
The update command left orphaned services running, outdated service files installed and new servers uninstalled because it never compared installed state to the repo.
The auto flow merged a PR and reported success without checking the post-merge CI pipeline, which had failed on a config parse error.
The diagram skill's examples passed host save paths to a containerised tool that cannot write them, so every documented call hit an error.
The C4 diagram skill produced a component diagram for only one container instead of one per container in multi-container projects.
Diagram generators embedded node labels and titles into HTML without escaping, allowing stored script injection from analysed project content.
Diagram colour palettes paired text and backgrounds that failed the accessibility contrast minimum.
A container kept running without API keys because it was created before the keys existed and compose did not refresh its environment on restart.
The container status skill template used shell features unsupported in the agent's shell, so every invocation failed once before the agent adapted.
The browser MCP server reported healthy yet rejected every tool call with an invalid-parameters error, with signs of stale connection handling.
Green PR checks did not reflect the deploy path, which still ran stale host-installed helper scripts, so a deploy failed only after merge.
Diagram relationship panels showed raw node IDs instead of labels and overflowed a fixed-height body, silently clipping edges.
An issue was closed by a commit while several checklist items were unfinished, leaving the init wizard guiding users to the superseded plaintext secrets path.
Generated skill wrappers had unquoted frontmatter values that were invalid YAML, so the consuming agent skipped all of them at startup.
The streamable HTTP endpoint returned 500 on every server because a lifespan task group was never initialised, while root health endpoints still reported healthy.
A merged commit introduced a return-type error that failed the type check and turned the main pipeline red.
The CI deploy step ran compose from the CI clone, where the gitignored environment file does not exist, so the stack failed to start on every relevant push.
The model catalog advertised four free-tier model IDs that were invalid or decommissioned at the provider, so calls to them always failed.
Requests sent a max-token value above one provider's ceiling at higher verbosity, silently dropping those models from multi-model panels.
The deployed secret lacked keys for the free-tier providers, so every free model in the catalog was unavailable through the normal path.
A red deploy exposed that updates never refreshed containers, conflicting deployment models coexisted, dry-run builds went green, and deploy targeted an arbitrary CI agent.
The update command pulled code and synced dependencies but never rebuilt or restarted running containers, leaving the live stack stale.
Stale and orphaned service units from an old deployment model coexisted with the serving containers, and the update step would restart the wrong ones.
CI persistently deployed the stack onto whichever agent it scheduled rather than where it is used, and its dry-run builds never ran the images.
A tight healthcheck window marked the secrets sidecar unhealthy under concurrent build load, aborting every dependent container and failing the pipeline.
A transient start baked empty credentials into the secrets sidecar, which crash-looped forever while dependent containers sat stuck with no logs.
Review found a chain where a keyless server passed a liveness-only healthcheck and replaced a working container, producing a green deploy of a dead service.
The secret-fetch entrypoint started the server keyless after fetch failures, treating missing secrets as acceptable and letting health checks pass.
Base images, the package tool and deployable images used moving tags, so a green build was not reproducible and could pull stale layers.
Healthchecks only probed liveness, so a server without secrets or failed initialisation was marked healthy and passed the release gate.
CI smoke tests exercised the local fallback instead of the production secret-fetch path, and never ran the images it built.
Source patches applied with sed succeed even when nothing matches, so an upstream reformat could silently drop a patch while the build and ping stay green.
The secrets sidecar was published to the host with a known default token and app containers received cloud credentials, widening exposure.
The Anthropic provider path called the API without streaming, so every detailed or in-depth request was refused by the SDK's duration limit.
Concurrent push and PR pipelines for one commit doubled unauthenticated image pulls and hit the registry rate limit, intermittently failing builds.
Smoke readiness probes failed on the first refused connection, producing frequent false failures on code that passed elsewhere.
CI never proved the real secrets agent could fetch a real secret, so a healthy agent status did not show the fetch path worked.
A CI step depended on another step with narrower path filters, so changes to certain files produced a dangling dependency and a pipeline config error on main.
Skills generated by a retired architecture remained installed globally with no source in the repo, surfacing in every session unmanaged.
The update command never detected orphaned installed skills, and its docs wrongly assumed installed skills were symlinks refreshed by pulling.
After an MCP server was removed from the repo, its container, image and registration stayed on machines because drift detection used a hardcoded list.
A newly disclosed high-severity CVE in a digest-pinned base image failed the image scan on every pipeline because the pin had not been rotated.
The documented delegate invocation did not redirect stdin, so in non-interactive contexts the child process waited for input forever.
A blanket ignore rule silently dropped a new file, the gate runner crashed in fresh worktrees and silently fell back, and an installed skill copy described a retired architecture.
The installed global flow skill copies were not updated with the repo commands, so real runs executed the old manual-worktree logic.
Merging with branch deletion from a linked worktree failed on the local checkout step after the remote merge succeeded, so a successful merge read as a failure.
A branch cut from an older main failed the squash-merge on conflicts, and the gate had run on the pre-merge tree rather than what would land.
The secrets scanner walked gitignored untracked local files and blocked the finish gate on credentials that could never be committed.
Friction signals were written relative to the worktree cwd and deleted with the worktree at cleanup, so the retro drained an empty main-repo buffer.
The stale-base guard fired only at merge time, so edits were made against files that concurrent sibling PRs had already changed.
Stale generated skills shadowed the live commands for weeks, and the drift checker reported them OK because their family was never listed as deprecated.
Permission-prompt capture relied on the model noticing approvals it cannot observe, so the class recorded zero signals and its retro step was starved.
The merge helper squash-merged while mergeability was still being computed, so a transient unknown state produced a false stop.
Absolute-path edits in a native worktree session landed in the main repo working tree instead of the worktree.
A database driver installed without its native backend made the memory client report the store unreachable, misattributing a local driver gap to an outage.
The runner invocation synced only main dependencies while a required library lived in a dev extra, so it died in fresh checkouts.
Very long single-line inventory entries in a shared doc caused repeated merge conflicts when concurrent PRs each appended to the same line.
A sibling PR merging between the mergeability poll and the squash made the merge fail because the base branch had been modified.
A second flow run could resume into a worktree another live session was mid-implementation in, risking one driver deleting the other's cwd.
The ignored-additions guard warned on every run about a file ignored by design, training operators to skim past its real warnings.
Merging main after a sibling changed command sources left generated plugin copies stale, failing the parity gate until regenerated by hand.
The flow command pointed at a repo-relative gate spec that did not exist in other repos, so runs silently used a thin inline summary instead.
The merge helper had no admin passthrough or protection-block detection, so every owner merge on a protected branch failed into a manual step.
An unbounded find in a drift script matched files inside sibling session worktrees, making a test flaky on a multi-session host.
The census hook derived its allow candidate from the leading cd segment, producing already-allowed noise and hiding the real prompt drivers.
The drift teardown removed live external server containers because their names matched a deprecated list, treating name as provenance.
The documented stale-base remedy said to merge before committing, which fails with uncommitted changes, so operators had to invert the order by hand.
The quality-gate runner failed under a restricted sandbox on cache writes, interpreter selection, inherited env and blocked network before running checks.
Deploying from a worktree derived a per-directory compose project, colliding with pinned container names and leaking volumes and networks.
The stale check printed a fetch failure when the fetch had succeeded, and the worktree guard warned on unrelated pre-existing dirt in the main checkout.
The finish runner's test step hung or timed out with no output, so a slow suite was indistinguishable from a real hang.
The census hook recorded interactive dialogs as permission friction, inflating counts and the pending-signal reminder with unfixable records.
The update command read the version from the first numbered changelog heading, reporting no version change for a real multi-commit upgrade.
A self-modifying update command kept executing its pre-pull steps after the pull changed it, including steps referencing deleted scripts.
The capture side never set the new harness tag, so every friction row landed unattributed and the per-harness split was empty.
The schema initializer split SQL naively on semicolons, so a semicolon inside a comment broke database initialization for every store.
The worktree removal helper exited non-zero after a squash-merge because the safe branch delete refused, so successful cleanup read as failure.
A plugin shipped an active pointer to an external server that is not running on fresh installs, so every install reported a load error.
When every edit leaked to the main tree, the worktree guard's edited set was empty, so the leak was downgraded to a pre-existing-dirt note.
Update and init never invoked several installers and teardowns, leaving hosts running stale retired prompts and frozen generated skills.
Several shipped drift guards were never run by CI, make or tests, so the invariants they protect went unchecked.
The flow start step assumed the session cwd was the target repo, so runs launched from a non-repo parent directory could not create the worktree.
The merge step treated a required-review block as mergeable and would proceed to a merge needing an admin bypass of owner review.
Top-level commands were excluded by the generators' discovery, so they shipped in no plugin and parity gates could not see the gap.
The flow plugin commands depended on helper scripts that only a clone-based installer provides, so marketplace-only installs hard-failed.
The vendored-core drift check was invoked by nothing, so upstream gate fixes could never be flagged as missing.
The start resolver inferred the session repo from the drifting shell cwd, emitting a lane decision for the wrong repo.
The deploy verification step used a broken interpreter and module path already fixed in an earlier step, so verification silently never ran.
When the session cwd was not a git repo, the resolver reported the native lane instead of the cross-repo lane its docs promised.
Concurrent flow sessions removed each other's worktrees, entered them mid-run, duplicated deploys and churned the base, with no cross-session claim.
The census hook emitted cat and bare git as allow candidates although the retro spec asserts the hook withholds them.
A test shelled out to git without a skip guard and failed in a CI image lacking git, the third breach of a written directive.
The deploy verification command was only string-matched by a doc test and never executed, so a broken invocation could survive undetected.
The next-issue report read dependencies from issue text only, and generated issue text had drifted from the spec, so a blocked issue was ranked ready.
The merge helper treated a not-protected 404 as a required check that never reported, false-stopping after a long wait and exiting 0 on refusal.
The stale-base check inspected whatever tree the shell cwd had drifted to and reported current while the actual worktree was behind.
Helpers moved to a stable bare path were not added to the shipped allowlist template, so they still prompted on every run.
The finish gate omitted typecheck and ignored project config, so it reported green on trees that CI rejected on type errors.
A schema requiring a port rejected a portless service config, the whole file failed validation, and fail-open verification silently never ran.
The test step judged success on exit code alone, so a run that skipped every relevant test reported the finish gate successful.
Installed plugin command text lagged the checkout by weeks with nothing detecting it, so sessions re-hit and re-filed already-fixed bugs.
The compose project pin covered only the deploy step, so other compose commands from a worktree built a parallel stack and leaked volumes.
The finish gate reported ok in a repo without a Makefile while skipping lint, test and typecheck entirely.
A shipped project config hardcoded a server port with no override, so the server was unreachable inside the repo on a host where that port was taken.
The drift check flagged images used by a live external stack as orphaned, nagging to remove images out from under running containers.
Concurrent sessions shared one git stash stack, so a bare pop applied another session's uncommitted work into the wrong worktree.
Session listing labels did not map to worker roles, so the orchestrator repeatedly sent assignments and probes to the wrong session.
Unattended quality gates in concurrent sessions each inherited an unbounded pytest worker pool, oversubscribing the shared host; the hazard note also misstated where parallelism came from.
The merge helper squashed without an explicit subject, so PRs whose first commit was a WIP commit landed on main titled WIP.
A recorded workaround of soft-resetting onto a moved base committed a stale index, silently reverting a sibling's merged feature while every check stayed green.
A drifted working directory made relative-pathspec diffs return empty, which read as no changes and produced confident wrong damage assessments.
The plugin update path compared unchanged version stamps, reported already-latest and left sessions executing a weeks-stale command cache with missing commands.
The update step symlinked only shell scripts, so a shipped allowlist rule for a Python helper pointed at a nonexistent path.
The registration protocol worked only when the orchestrator registered first, so a worker registering earlier had no path to a verified address and stalled.
A worker registering without a wave name landed silently in a default wave while the orchestrator's roster showed empty, and both sides reported success.
Address self-derivation walked a socket directory that current harness versions no longer create, so it could never succeed and wave addressing could not bootstrap.
A drift checker treated a permission-denied container listing as an empty host and reported clean, which was relayed to other sessions as a positive finding.
The verify step flagged a benign fill of an unknown address with the same mismatch warning as a real conflict, so the flag fired on every worker.
Registration docs described addressing as socket-only while the implementation accepted any transport token, leading a worker to conclude a working wave was broken.
The wave protocol assumed orchestrator-to-worker session messaging that the harness lacks, so an assignment sat undelivered for hours until a human relayed it.
The helper installer omitted one script, so its shipped stable-path allowlist rule matched nothing outside the interactive init path and fallbacks prompted.
Sessions registering from a shared parent directory produced false worktree-collision warnings against every live role, burying real overlap signal.
A link check reported ok on a corrupted working tree because it verified symlink topology only, while every served command was stale.
A help option printed a hardcoded line range that ran past the doc comment, emitting executable source after the help text.
The wave roster ignored worktree claim locks, so an issue claimed by an unregistered live session appeared unclaimed and nearly got double-assigned.
A secondary liveness proof stripped a socket-scheme prefix that non-socket addresses lack, so it silently never fired while docs described a two-factor rule.
Re-registering the same session at the same address reset its verified flag, so the roster showed actively-messaged workers as unverified.
Routine re-registration cleared a genuine address-mismatch flag, erasing an uninvestigated misrouting signal so the entry rendered clean.
A fail-open test fixture emptied PATH, removing far more than the intended tool, so its assertions could pass while proving nothing.
Tab-delimited records read with tab as IFS collapsed empty fields, shifting later fields and corrupting branch and worktree matching for branchless claims.
A second script parsed tab-delimited records with tab IFS, latently shifting fields on an empty first field, safe only by an unrecorded input invariant.
A test built its command from the interpreter path, so a checkout path containing the word test flipped a heuristic and turned the test red spuriously.
A validator enforced worker-side message shapes that were documented only on the orchestrator side, so workers were refused by a rule they were never shown.
The merge helper's fixed check-poll window counted from poll start, so under CI queue load it expired on queued pipelines and looked like a failed merge.
PR bodies that disclaimed closing an issue still contained the closing-keyword pattern, so partial-delivery merges auto-closed issues twice despite a memorized rule.
A delegated implementation agent read repo workflow docs and autonomously committed, pushed, opened a PR and attempted a merge nobody authorized.
The start resolver reported no PR head on the remote-pickup lane despite an open PR for the branch, likely querying outside the target repo, so the duplicate-PR guard never fired.
The delegated CLI version could not parse reasoning fields in the local model's streaming chunks and hung indefinitely waiting for content.
The local-model auto skill passed a wall-time flag that the installed CLI does not support, so execution failed before starting.
The default sandbox container lacked the host's private network, so a remote model endpoint the skill documents was unreachable from it.
The update command had no coverage of the local-model tiers, so harness versions and the permission-fence profile on installed hosts never refreshed.
Status commands reported the model server unreachable when its endpoint variable was simply never persisted, misdirecting diagnosis toward a healthy server.
The link check collapsed a missing new command family and a link to another checkout into one drift verdict, so new families stayed unreachable behind a prompt.
The update step's prose hardcoded a family-link count that had drifted twice as new command families shipped.
Help text presented auto and exec as a capability pair without saying auto requires an existing repo and issue, so greenfield requests hit an unexplained error.
Scaffolded projects told users to create a venv with the stdlib module, which fails on stock Debian-family hosts and leaves a half-built environment.
Ad-hoc CI verification grepped a shared pipeline list and reported another concurrent session's failed pipeline as this run's result.
The merge helper checked the base only before a multi-minute status-check wait, so a base that advanced meanwhile produced a merge-conflict failure at merge time.
Improvised CI polling matched an unrelated concurrent pipeline and reported a queued run as failed, while another poll grepped a table format that never matched.
The local finish gate declared failure on the first non-zero test exit, so host-state-sensitive flaky tests halted runs that passed on an immediate re-run.
The negated-close guard matched any negation anywhere earlier in the sentence, refusing merges whose negation belonged to an unrelated clause.
Three delegated drivers printed a plan report that looked like a gate and then implemented in the same turn with no pause for approval.
A trailer in an issue body or the HEAD commit message silently auto-approved the pre-implementation gate for every later run branched from that tip.
The roster showed a registered, verified worker as healthy while its mailbox watch was never armed, so its assignment went unread for over an hour.
Nothing checked driver capability before assignment, so research and web-dependent issues were routed to drivers whose fences structurally forbid that work.
Delegated drivers' approval gates kept a pre-plan skip flag that had been removed from the main gate, and a test asserted the escape hatch existed.
A test binary-guard checker only saw literal argv in Python sources, so a test reaching an unshipped tool through a shell script passed locally and went red in CI.
The mailbox watch consumed every unread message while showing one, duplicate watchers competed for mail, and its status could not distinguish a healthy re-arm gap from a blind role.
The start resolver reported a fresh lane but silently checked out a pre-existing local branch of the same name, discarding the base ref and landing on another worker's unmerged tip.
Closing keywords used incidentally near an issue reference in PR bodies and inline commit subjects would close issues, a shape the negation guard did not see.
Delegated-model lanes tested an exit status masked by a tee pipeline or captured in a separate shell, so timeouts and API errors read as successful runs.
A re-registration that omitted the repo cleared the scoping key, so a role with a declared file lane dropped out of overlap detection and the roster read clean.
The watch status reported armed from a stale heartbeat while no watcher process was running, and one-shot watches left sessions silently deaf for tens of minutes.
The finish gate auto-resumed a failed run after a source fix, skipping lint and tests on the changed tree and reporting ok, then deleted the resume evidence.
The merge helper treated a stale pre-push conflicting mergeability value as authoritative and hard-stopped a PR that had no conflicts.
The finish-gate fallback ran three of a repo's nine gate targets and reported ok without naming them, and exited success when it ran nothing at all.
Concurrent merges kept moving the base during the check wait, so the base-move guard's refusal sent sessions back into the same race repeatedly.
The finish gate ran a suite as one invocation where the project deliberately splits it, manufacturing setup errors, while also resuming stale runs and under-counting tests.
A mailbox watch exited after each delivery or timeout with no successor listener, leaving persisted assignments unheard whenever an agent missed a re-arm.
Mailbox reads advanced the read cursor on output rather than on recipient receipt, and the durable-copy option advanced it even when the copy write failed.
Command docs set PYTHONPATH one level too deep, which worked only from the project root, because an earlier contract migration fixed 13 sites and missed 57.
Two further documented invocations could not reach the package, one with an unresolved variable and one with no path at all, and the new tripwire could not see either.
The watcher counter treated orphaned subshells of a killed watcher as live watchers, so a later watch refused to arm and tests failed intermittently.
An installed skill tree was an unrefreshed copy carrying weeks-old fixed bugs, while the drift detector watched a retired channel and a clean scan was read as fix-live.
The install drift check iterated only installed helpers, so a helper the repo shipped but never installed was invisible and the check reported ok.
The test binary-guard checker enforced guards for only four named binaries, so a test using an unlisted tool absent from the CI image passed locally and went red in CI.
The binary-guard checker read a shell case label as a command invocation, latent until the guarded set widened, when it would produce over a hundred false findings.
Eighteen detectors across two repos answered a narrow question while their readers took the answer as a broader one, including vacuous zeros over empty populations.
The driver capability matrix had no container-runtime axis, so container work routed to a driver whose fence denies it produced a clean-looking success with nothing done.
The delegated-run checker reported success from a clean exit and a tool-use event even when the tool call was denied and the requested work never happened.
The binary-guard checker also read variable assignments and names inside quoted strings as command invocations, producing hundreds of latent false findings.
The binary-guard gate exited success when there was no tests directory, so scanning nothing was indistinguishable from everything being guarded.
A sweep found two more required gates that exit success with a universal all-clear on present-but-empty input, having examined zero items.
A fix keying watcher counts to the mailbox directory landed in one scan lane only, so the fallback lane still counted another mailbox's same-named watchers as ours.
Merge with branch deletion failed when a sibling worktree held the branch, orphaning local and remote branches, because the guard only inspected the invoking worktree.
The merge helper's zero exit meant only that the merge happened, so callers trusting it could not tell a fully cleaned-up merge from one with incomplete cleanup.
The spec-to-issue converter ignored bold task IDs from its own template and treated another feature's same-numbered task issue as satisfying the current one.
The supervising daemon consumed and acknowledged mail into a discarded output, so every deafness signal read clean while the agent behind the role had received nothing.
Liveness check treated a leftover socket file as proof a session was live after the pid had already been reported dead.
Delivery-lane preference order rested on a harness measurement that had expired, so docs routed messages on an obsolete constraint.
Supervise daemon acknowledged mail the model never saw, and those acks kept the route-health signal green while delivery was dead.
Driver capability check reported a delegated driver as fit for repo-meta issues its execution fence structurally forbids it to read.
A test assumed it owned the whole host process table, so a concurrent worktree watcher turned unrelated runs red.
Tests used a hardcoded host-global namespace over a whole-host process scan, so concurrent runs in different worktrees failed each other.
No step owned worktree teardown after merge, so every merged branch left its worktree behind and a routine warning was ignored.
A worktree actively used by a live session reported its claim as free because it was unlocked, letting a forced removal delete its work.
Security scan was missing from the gate-step list, so a skipped security gate reported ok instead of warning.
A repo value that did not resolve to a directory silently disabled claim reconciliation, with results depending on the reader working directory.
Delegated run check ignored nested error items, so a run whose execution tool never started was reported as success.
Local-model lane preflight checked only daemon and registration, so it passed against a host that could not actually serve the model.
A load-bearing comment asserted the harness cannot re-invoke an agent on background completion, but the installed harness can.
Worktree removal deleted uncommitted work on an idle worktree when forced, and never checked for unpushed commits.
Finish-gate retry treated a pass in isolation as a flake and marked the step success, hiding a real order-dependent failure.
Process scan used truncated argv, so a live watcher under a long checkout path was reported as a confident zero.
Binary-guard scan followed only bash-prefixed invocations, so tests running repo scripts directly were never scanned and eleven of twelve were missed.
Model-presence preflight matched a name prefix, so it passed when only a different model sharing the prefix was registered.
Retry reported the original failure as reproduced from the invocation exit code, although the retried test passed and a different test failed.
Unpushed-commit check read every squash-merged branch as unpushed once its remote tracking ref was deleted, refusing routine removals.
Serveability preflight result was trusted indefinitely although serving health was observed to change within minutes.
Two pinned dev dependencies carried known advisories that no issue tracked, after a scanner under-reported the lockfile.
Several gates returned confident verdicts they could not justify, and nothing proved any gate could report the failing verdict.
A known blind spot in the binary-guard scan let a displaced skip decorator leave tests unguarded, turning the pipeline red.
Repair command ran the stale installed installer it was meant to repair, so it installed nothing new and reported ok.
Negative-fixture check claimed to cover every constructed absence but detected only one path-replacement shape, overstating its coverage.
Opt-in cross-model review stage had never run on any of the last 200 merged changes.
The only secret-scanning gate had no committed case proving it could flag a planted credential.
Process-scan lane reported unknown whenever any default-wave watcher existed, displacing a meaningful dead verdict in the common case.
Test-summary parser read only the first stream that produced a summary, so failures reported on stderr were never retried or misread.
A subproject lockfile still carried many packages with known advisories after a partial dependency bump.
Docs described a mount configuration outcome as a hard boundary, after container sessions saw zero local peers.
Negative-control harness scored a crashing gate as detection when the crash exit code matched the detection code, reporting pass.
A documented vantage check could not distinguish a container from a lone host session and failed toward the wrong routing lane.
The negative-control checker was absent from both registers, so the register could not be read as a coverage map.
A control battery cleared by inspection kept passing when each protection it advertised was removed, so it was decorative.
Adopting shellcheck at error severity left a backlog of unreviewed lower-severity findings across many shell scripts.
The guarded worktree-removal fix landed in one command doc only, leaving a raw forced removal fallback on the more used path.
PR watcher reported on the highest-numbered pipeline regardless of status context, so its green could describe a lane the merge rule did not name.
Negative-control checker reported pass from untracked control files that would be absent in a clean clone.
Checker reported a count of discriminating controls with no denominator, so two and sixty-one controlled instruments read identically as ok.
Lexicon parser treated quoted tokens as issued, so a message retracting a gate would re-record that gate as a live verdict.
A closing keyword closed an issue with half its scope undelivered, leaving an instrument missing from the governing enumeration.
Restoring a stale snapshot after a soft reset pushed a commit that reverted another worker merged work, and no gate noticed.
Control discovery registered only the first control per gate, so extra controls were never run and the gate was certified by one.
The verify target gained a hard dependency on a linter declared nowhere, so a clean clone could not pass its own gate.
Under strict branch protection the main branch was an unmodelled serialized resource, so the longest-verifying PR was repeatedly overtaken.
Argument loops using an unguarded double shift spun forever when a value-taking flag was passed last, including in control fixtures.
A guard's could-not-look answer shared the clean exit code, so an undeterminable result read as no leak found.
Skipped reviews were recorded under reasons that conflated no diff, a human opt-out and inability to run, so a skip misreported why review did not happen.
Command docs still named a retired command as the consumer of a review contract that another step now parses.
Update command reported a harness upgrade from the installer exit code while an engine constraint left the version unchanged.
The list verb was not updated for a new capability axis, so it aborted per row and reported no incapacity for any driver.
Re-registering a role replaced its declared file lane silently, and the lane-extend verb actually replaced rather than extended the lane.
Every warn verdict of the finish gate exited zero, so the documented exit-code grading method could not see gates that did not run.
Several checkers sat outside the local verify target or could not run on one surface, so a local green said nothing about them.
Sessions executed helpers from a stale shared checkout and deleted-inode processes, with nothing able to report which version was running.
Pre-PR review diff omitted untracked new files, the stage lacked finding routing, and its receipt was written after the gate needing it.
A soft reset onto a moving shared ref turned sibling merged work into deletions, and the pre-push deletion check missed blank-line deletions.
Worktree ownership records such as ownerless locks, directory names and recycled pids were treated as identity when deciding removal safety.
An orphaned child held the supervisor lock so re-arming reported duplicate while the role stayed deaf, among other silent-deafness paths.
Skill validation lacked spec rules, so every skill name violated the spec, triggers sat in an unread key, and mirror checking was opt-in.
Next-issue ranking recommended a permanent inbox issue and a charting seed as startable work, and read its map from a missing path.
Control coverage fraction mixed independently derived counts, a non-homogeneous denominator and top-level-only discovery, overstating coverage.
Always-read documents stated facts nothing checked, including a wrong current version and an incomplete canonical document list.
A tracked script imported a package declared in no dependency metadata, so it failed under the project environment and escaped advisory scans.
Dependency audit adapter passed when its tool was absent, audited the ambient environment instead of the project, and hid parse failures.
Command docs named a reviewer model and settings that were no longer configured, and a receipt example copied that stale name.
Review receipts had to be written on a skip but required a reviewer name, forcing the skip path to fabricate a reviewer or fail.
Review receipts hardcoded the implementer model, so the reviewer-differs-from-implementer property was asserted rather than measured.
Every review receipt recorded the same caller-supplied reviewer value copied from a doc example, so the field could not distinguish models.
Tool-error counter matched a field the codex event stream never emits, so it always reported zero errors and the run as success.
A shared stash stack across worktrees restored another session uncommitted work, because the fix was a doc convention not covering all paths.
Instrument census membership was hand-appended, so a new instrument could ship unenumerated with no red from any check.
A script documented as always present was not executable, so installer loops that link only executables never installed it on fresh hosts.
A test scanned the whole host process table, so an unrelated session's watcher process turned the suite red.
Registry liveness treated any process with a recorded PID as the registered role, so a recycled PID made a dead role read alive.
A supervise daemon kept polling indefinitely after every role in its wave had ended, leaving a stray process running.

guard: slate reconciler with committed red cases
summary: A reconciler kept only in a session scratchpad was lost on resume, so later tracking counts looked reconciled but were not.
Receipt writer took the last model field anywhere in a transcript, so a nested tool argument could be recorded as the implementer and still validate.
The gate numbered waiver lines with a different line-splitting rule than it used for sites, so waivers shifted and produced false reds or silent exemptions.
Adopting a security linter surfaced eleven medium-or-higher findings such as shell=True with config strings and hard-coded temp paths, accepted as residual.
Tests leaked detached daemons that survived the run and pinned their worktree open, blocking cleanup.
The local verify run executed the whole control battery but read one verdict, and tool-absent and silent-gate outcomes shared one verdict.
The control register could not express a case for a gate's unknown branch, so that branch scored as unsignalled and could never be controlled.
Install and update commands wrote host surfaces that a managed environment owns read-only, with no way to be told which surfaces to leave alone.
A re-sync trigger looked only at command documents, so edits to bundled docs drifted generated mirrors while the trigger stayed silent.
The init command checked for a checkout rather than the installed tool, then a link helper resolved the wrong source and reported ok with nothing linked.
The init command appended a prompt export to the shell rc file without a guard, so each re-run duplicated it.
A fixture kept requiring a sentence removed from the docs, so the local verify went red on main while CI, which never ran that check, stayed green.
Ten local verify gates had no CI invocation, so merges consumed a green that never ran them.
The finish gate ran three of the verify target's gates yet was treated as the full verify verdict, and its post-merge backstop shared the same blindness.
A sync check named mirror paths only after drift, so on a clean tree it listed nothing and was misread as an empty mirror set.
The declared gate set and the executed plan came from different files, so an added gate was declared but never run while the gate printed ok.
An anchor predating a gate's refusal branch could never agree on an unknown case, so the harness scored it inert and the case could not be registered.
Generated manifests pointed the deploy plan at the finish security policy, so high-severity findings no longer blocked a deploy.
A Makefile parser ignored backslash continuations, returning a truncated prerequisite list ending in a literal backslash.
Controls reaching a Python package could not run in the CI control image, and a read-only filesystem failure could be scored as a detection.
Gate deduplication matched step ids against a textual prerequisite list, so a disabled or differently defined check could be marked covered without running.
A resumed run lost which gates had been deferred to the aggregate, so a successful retry was rejected as having unrun gates.
A dependency check for CI controls examined binaries and shebangs but not Python imports, so it passed a control that could not import in CI.
A skipped cross-model review wrote no receipt and simply shrank the population, so it was indistinguishable from a clean review.
A gate crashed on unparseable files, and the obvious guard turned that into a green that counted unparsed files as scanned.
A sandboxed-home observation harness could write to the real home through three routes, so its containment claim exceeded what it enforced.
The install path compared installed helpers only to their source, so a tampered bundled helper installed with a success verdict.
The verdict ledger dropped a hold's reason written beneath the token while reporting success, and could not record rulings on issueless work.
Helper contract lines returned plausible wrong values, including failures echoed by a control being reported as real pipeline failures.
A PR using only a reference keyword closed its issue because a heading ending in close preceded the issue number, and the guard missed it.
Gate deduplication refused any Makefile with an include, so its intended consumer never benefited, and the refusal printed nothing.
The update command called a helper that was absent, and each step printed an unconditional success line after the write failed.
A secret-masking hook was declared in a file the harness never reads, so it never fired while docs claimed the protection was active.
Command substitution stripped NUL separators, so multiple untracked files merged into one path and the plan comparison went unknown.
New worktree branches tracked the default branch, so a bare push failed and git's first suggested remedy pushed to the default branch.
Releasing a role kept its issue, PR, branch and file lane, so the shared roster showed stale claims for ended sessions.
A tripwire recognised only one exact spelling of an invocation, so flagged or commented calls escaped both lists silently.
Two CI lanes gave different verdicts on one commit because a test lacked a git guard while the code it called needed git.
Docs prescribed a detached listener daemon that cannot wake its session, so sessions went deaf while the roster showed them armed.
A test ran the real install against the user's home with a fixture source, deleting most installed skills while passing.
The install copied then pruned in place, so a concurrent reader saw skills with missing files mid-install.
Docs still described a retired sibling project as active, and a dormancy checklist had met criteria left unticked.
Ignored bytecode files under a control counted as untracked, so every second local verify run failed falsely.
Tests each re-ran the whole control battery and hit a fixed timeout under load, making CI intermittently red.
A module-level cache kept a value computed under a monkeypatched table, so a later test failed depending on worker ordering.
Tests inherited the launching session's process lineage, so seven failed locally while CI passed.
A service was defined at two scopes with different endpoints, while the drift checks reported OK because they only checked registration.
The unmapped-worktree message was identical for delivered and undelivered work, so cleanup could not be decided.
Start and finish gates let work through: a worktree was created before confirmation, a verdict printed without exiting and a warning exited zero.
The control harness could score a crashed anchor as detected, stale bytecode could mask a mutation, and a shared recipe could be dropped.
Messaging stored a literal dash as a body while reporting delivery, recreated directories it inspected, and read an unreadable registry as empty.
Delegated review lanes reviewed less than reported, via a read-only sandbox, wrong upstream tracking and a lost enumeration exit status.
CI status and merge helpers misreported: wrong default lane, expired waits read as unregistered, and truncated file lists read as violations.
Update and drift tools left dangling links, reported the pulled rather than final commit, and did not resync mirrors, all unreported.
Security modules still routed a missing scanner binary to skipped rather than unknown, and the control harness saw only top-level scripts.
A run checker silently reported zero beyond a fixed nesting depth and counted unparseable lines as recognised.
The shared registry computed lane changes outside its write lock and kept stale facts across re-registration.
Plan compliance mapped generated manifests and some mirrors to wrong or nonexistent sources, producing false divergence.
The census parser read any numbered table row as a census row, did not check row uniqueness, and one row named the wrong consumer.
Review receipts recorded reviewer identity with no evidence pointer, some reviews had no receipt and one branch had duplicates.
Tests leaked daemons, depended on the host's session lineage and scanned whole working trees, colliding across parallel runs.
Several docs and contracts described behaviour and counts that main no longer had.
A sweep of low-severity findings included duplicated rules, stale citations and outdated examples across docs.
The control harness could only register gates that are top-level script files, so other gates were uncountable while coverage read as complete.
A self-test mutated a model of the instrument rather than its source, overreporting two protections as caught.
A hard-coded sandbox mode could not start in containers, so the delegated tool exited zero and changed nothing.
Secret-scan failures printed the detected secret value into scanner output and test diagnostics.
Framework detection dropped nested stacks when a root manifest existed and gave Django without a lockfile no runners.
A test-step classifier matched a test token in the checkout path, so a non-test step drew a warn verdict in some directories.
A test fixture signalled its child before the child had installed its signal trap, giving intermittent CI failures.
The classifier missed a test runner inside a quoted shell command and treated an environment assignment as a test hint.
A security scan ignored the target repo's secret-scan allowlist, blocking on planted fixtures so every run overrode the gate.
With several sessions merging into one repo, CI outlasted the base's quiet window and the merge helper stopped repeatedly.
A global skill the workflow reads first was never installed, so every run outside the source repo fell back to a manual read.
Load-sensitive tests asserted effects before asynchronous actions finished or hit a fixed timeout, turning CI red on unrelated PRs.
A pipeline tee process re-created a temp file after the exit trap removed it, leaking the file when the gate was killed under load.
A second workflow run on an issue was satisfied by the first run's committed approval, bypassing its own plan approval.
A test mapped heading count words through a fixed dictionary, so correct index growth failed as an unrecognised word.
The security scan examined the runner's own state files, an assert vanished under optimisation and a test fixture anchored on the wrong root.
A CI status helper could not distinguish a clone-step failure from a code failure, and a freshness report omitted HEAD's age.
The suite leaked an orphaned child process and inherited an environment variable that made tests red in containers.
A new cleanup test failed on unreadable processes of parallel workers and leaked its own fixture when it failed.
A version consistency check never read the lockfile, so a missed re-lock would ship two versions while the check stayed green.
A control judged a resume case by exit code alone, so a different warning passed and a resume regression could hide.
Helpers needing network ran inside a no-network sandbox and reported a misleading connection error.
A locked dependency version gained three new CVEs, turning the dependency audit red on every main push.
The finish gate summary counted expected failures as failed inside a success verdict.
